Rule_Name: CPU DNN Performance Must Be Evaluated With the Target Software Stack
Rule_Description: When assessing CPU capability for DNN training, evaluate the target model together with CPU architecture, optimized libraries, and threading configuration rather than treating hardware specifications alone as workload throughput.
Inputs: Target DNN/model; CPU architecture; software/library stack; thread configuration
Condition: CPU configuration is being assessed for DNN training
Output_Decision: Profile/evaluate the candidate with the target workload and software stack.
Paper_Title: An In-depth Performance Characterization of CPU- and GPU-based DNN Training on Modern Architectures
Authors: Ammar Ahmad Awan; Hari Subramoni; Dhabaleswar K. Panda
Research_Evidence: The study evaluates CPU DNN training across architectures and software stacks and discusses the effects of hardware features and optimized libraries.
Applicability: DNN training workloads evaluated through CPU-based execution.
Limitations: No universal CPU-throughput equation; results remain workload/framework/hardware dependent.

Rule_Name: Optimized CPU Libraries and Thread Parallelism Must Be Considered Before Judging CPU Training Capacity
Rule_Description: If CPU-based DNN training is selected, optimized CPU kernels/libraries and thread parallelism should be considered as configuration variables before declaring the CPU configuration insufficient.
Inputs: CPU architecture; optimized library availability; thread configuration; target DNN
Condition: CPU DNN training is evaluated with configurable software optimization
Output_Decision: Evaluate optimized library/thread configurations before rejecting CPU capacity.
Paper_Title: An In-depth Performance Characterization of CPU- and GPU-based DNN Training on Modern Architectures
Authors: Ammar Ahmad Awan; Hari Subramoni; Dhabaleswar K. Panda
Research_Evidence: The paper reports substantial CPU-training improvement from optimized MKL-DNN/MKL designs and OpenMP-based thread parallelism compared with under-optimized configurations.
Applicability: CPU DNN training using software stacks where such optimization libraries/threading are available.
Limitations: Reported gains are configuration-specific and must not become universal speedup factors.

Rule_Name: CPU Memory Configuration Can Affect DNN Training Performance
Rule_Description: For CPU platforms exposing multiple memory configurations, memory mode/placement should be treated as a CPU-performance configuration variable during DNN training evaluation.
Inputs: CPU memory configuration; target DNN; CPU platform
Condition: The CPU platform provides alternative memory configurations
Output_Decision: Evaluate the applicable memory configuration rather than assuming equivalent CPU performance across modes.
Paper_Title: An In-depth Performance Characterization of CPU- and GPU-based DNN Training on Modern Architectures
Authors: Ammar Ahmad Awan; Hari Subramoni; Dhabaleswar K. Panda
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: p. 4, §4.3.2, Impact of MCDRAM for Training on KNL; Fig. 4
Research_Evidence: The KNL experiment compares MCDRAM cache/allocation modes with DDR-only allocation and reports different DNN-training performance trends.
Applicability: CPU platforms with multiple memory modes, especially the evaluated KNL/MCDRAM configuration.
Limitations: Platform-specific; no universal memory-mode performance factor.

Rule_Name: Data Loading Must Be Treated as a Potential Training Bottleneck
Rule_Description: For training workloads, data-loading time and throughput should be profiled because the input pipeline can materially affect overall training time and accelerator utilization.
Inputs: Data-loading time; loader throughput; training time; accelerator activity
Output_Decision: Include data-loading performance in CPU-side training analysis.
Paper_Title: Accelerating Data Loading in Deep Neural Network Training; Importance of Data Loading Pipeline in Training Deep Neural Networks
Authors: Chih-Chieh Yang; Guojing Cong; Mahdi Zolnouri; Xinlin Li; Vahid Partovi Nia
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Yang & Cong: pp. 235-245, Abstract/analytical-model discussion; Zolnouri et al.: pp. 51-58, Abstract/§1
Research_Evidence: Both studies identify data loading as a potentially significant contributor to training time; Yang & Cong also analyze scalability limitations.
Applicability: Large-scale/distributed DNN training and training workloads with substantial input preprocessing.
Limitations: No universal fraction of training time or universal CPU requirement is established.

Rule_Name: Distributed Training Scalability Must Consider Input I/O Limits
Rule_Description: If distributed-training scaling is limited by the input pipeline, evaluate I/O rate and data-loading scalability before attributing the bottleneck to CPU compute capacity.
Inputs: I/O rate; data-loading throughput; distributed-training scale; CPU resources
Condition: Distributed training is being scaled and input-pipeline performance is material
Output_Decision: Classify the limiting resource using measured I/O/data-loading evidence.
Paper_Title: Accelerating Data Loading in Deep Neural Network Training
Research_Evidence: The paper states that I/O rate can limit distributed-training scalability and motivates locality-aware data loading.
Limitations: I/O limitation is workload/system dependent and is not a universal CPU bottleneck.

Rule_Name: Online Data Augmentation Must Be Included in CPU Input-Pipeline Analysis
Rule_Description: When training includes computationally intensive online data augmentation, include augmentation/preprocessing cost in CPU input-pipeline analysis.
Inputs: Augmentation operations; preprocessing time; data-loading throughput
Output_Decision: Evaluate CPU preprocessing/input-pipeline capacity and its effect on training throughput.
Paper_Title: Importance of Data Loading Pipeline in Training Deep Neural Networks; A parallel framework for data input pipelines and online data augmentation in deep learning
Authors: Mahdi Zolnouri; Xinlin Li; Vahid Partovi Nia; Antonio De Toro-Castro; Marcos Lupión; Vicente González-Ruiz; Juan F. Sanjuan; Pilar M. Ortigosa
Venue: Edge Intelligence Workshop 2020; The Journal of Supercomputing 2026
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: P3: pp. 51-58, Abstract/§1; P6: Abstract; §1/architecture description
Research_Evidence: P3 identifies augmentation as increasing data-loading demand; P6 presents parallel CPU loading/preprocessing and online augmentation.
Applicability: Training pipelines with nontrivial online augmentation.
Limitations: No universal worker count or preprocessing-core requirement is established.

Rule_Name: CPU Input Production May Require Decoupled Producer-Consumer Design
Rule_Description: When CPU input production limits training, a decoupled/buffered producer-consumer design should be considered and validated against measured pipeline throughput.
Inputs: CPU preprocessing rate; consumer rate; buffering/shared-memory design
Condition: Input production is slower than or competes with consumption
Output_Decision: Consider decoupled/buffered input-pipeline architecture and validate throughput.
Paper_Title: A parallel framework for data input pipelines and online data augmentation in deep learning
Authors: Antonio De Toro-Castro; Marcos Lupión; Vicente González-Ruiz; Juan F. Sanjuan; Pilar M. Ortigosa
Research_Evidence: The proposed framework decouples data production from consumption using multiprocessing and global shared memory/ring-buffer architecture.
Limitations: An architectural pattern from the studied framework, not a universal requirement.

Rule_Name: NUMA-Aware CPU and Data Placement Should Be Considered on Multi-Socket DNN Systems
Rule_Description: For DNN workloads running on NUMA-based multi-socket CPUs, evaluate CPU/thread and data placement because remote NUMA accesses can increase memory latency and hurt scalability.
Inputs: NUMA topology; CPU/thread placement; data placement; remote-memory access indicators
Output_Decision: Prefer or validate NUMA-aware placement when remote-access behavior is material.
Paper_Title: NUMA-Caffe: NUMA-Aware Deep Learning Neural Networks
Authors: Probir Roy; Shuaiwen Leon Song; Sriram Krishnamoorthy; Abhinav Vishnu; Debabrata Sengupta; X. Liu
Venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization
Research_Evidence: The paper identifies remote NUMA memory accesses as a source of long memory latency and poor scalability and proposes NUMA-aware DNN design.
Applicability: Multi-/many-core NUMA CPU architectures and DNN workloads.
Limitations: No universal NUMA penalty percentage should be inferred.

Rule_Name: NUMA Optimization Must Be Validated for the Target Problem Size
Rule_Description: When using NUMA-related thread/data-mapping optimizations, do not assume a configuration optimized for one problem size remains optimal for another; validate or retune it for the target size.
Inputs: Problem size; NUMA mapping; thread mapping; measured performance/energy
Condition: A NUMA optimization is transferred across problem sizes
Output_Decision: Validate or retune the NUMA configuration for the target problem size.
Paper_Title: Optimizing performance and energy across problem sizes through a search space exploration and machine learning
Authors: Lana Scravaglieri; Mihail Popov; Laércio Lima Pilla; Amina Guermouche; Olivier Aumage; Emmanuelle Saillard
Venue: Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing
Research_Evidence: The study reports that optimization strategies do not transfer perfectly across problem sizes and that gains vary with problem size.
Applicability: NUMA/prefetch configuration optimization in the evaluated HPC setting.
Limitations: Reported transfer percentages are configuration-specific and are not universal factors.

Rule_Name: NUMA Configuration Should Be Tuned for the Actual Optimization Objective
Rule_Description: If the CPU configuration is being optimized for energy rather than performance, do not automatically reuse a performance-optimal NUMA/prefetch configuration; objective-specific validation is required.
Inputs: Optimization objective; NUMA mapping; prefetch configuration; measured performance/energy
Output_Decision: Select or validate configuration against the actual optimization objective.
Paper_Title: Optimizing performance and energy across problem sizes through a search space exploration and machine learning
Authors: Lana Scravaglieri; Mihail Popov; Laércio Lima Pilla; Amina Guermouche; Olivier Aumage; Emmanuelle Saillard
Venue: Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing
Research_Evidence: The paper reports that configurations optimized for performance do not necessarily transfer to energy optimization.
Limitations: No universal performance-energy tradeoff is asserted.

Rule_Name: CPU Memory Bandwidth Must Be Treated as Problem-Size and Thread Dependent
Rule_Description: For NUMA CPU workloads where memory bandwidth is material, characterize bandwidth using workload/problem size and thread count rather than a single fixed bandwidth-per-core value.
Inputs: Transferred data; execution time; problem size; thread count; NUMA configuration
Condition: Memory bandwidth is a relevant performance constraint
Output_Decision: Use measured or predicted bandwidth for the target problem-size/thread configuration.
Paper_Title: Memory Bandwidth Prediction in NUMA Architecture Using Supervised Machine Learning
Research_Evidence: The paper expresses memory bandwidth as transferred data per execution time and uses problem size and thread count as prediction features.
Applicability: NUMA architectures and the evaluated HPC applications.
Limitations: Prediction quality depends on training-data coverage; no universal bandwidth-per-core rule.

Rule_Name: UVM On-Demand Paging Should Be Checked as a CPU-GPU Data-Movement Bottleneck
Rule_Description: When a workload uses CPU-GPU unified virtual memory with on-demand page migration, evaluate page-table-walk and data-migration overhead before attributing performance loss to CPU compute.
Inputs: UVM usage; page migration; CPU-GPU interconnect activity; access locality
Condition: CPU-GPU UVM uses on-demand page movement
Output_Decision: Profile page-migration/data-movement behavior as a possible bottleneck.
Paper_Title: Deep Learning based Data Prefetching in CPU-GPU Unified Virtual Memory
Authors: Xinjian Long; Xiangyang Gong; Bo Zhang; Huiyang Zhou
Venue: Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing
Research_Evidence: The paper identifies on-demand UVM paging as a performance bottleneck because of page-table walks and data migration over the interconnect.
Limitations: Does not establish a general CPU bottleneck for non-UVM systems.

Rule_Name: Aggressive UVM Prefetching Requires Validation Under Device-Memory Oversubscription
Rule_Description: If UVM prefetching is used while device memory may be oversubscribed, validate that the policy does not induce page eviction or thrashing that offsets its benefit.
Inputs: Device-memory occupancy; prefetch policy; page eviction; interconnect traffic
Condition: Device memory is oversubscribed or near capacity
Output_Decision: Avoid unvalidated aggressive prefetching and test for eviction/thrashing.
Paper_Title: Deep Learning based Data Prefetching in CPU-GPU Unified Virtual Memory
Authors: Xinjian Long; Xiangyang Gong; Bo Zhang; Huiyang Zhou
Venue: Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing
Research_Evidence: The paper warns that aggressive prefetching under GPU-memory oversubscription can force eviction and cause page-thrashing overhead.
Limitations: No universal prefetch threshold is established.

Rule_Name: CPU Inference Threading Has Diminishing Returns
Rule_Description: For CPU-based DNN serving, increasing intra-operator thread parallelism must be treated as a measured configuration choice because additional threads can provide diminishing latency returns.
Inputs: DNN model; batch size; thread count; latency
Condition: CPU-based online inference is being configured
Output_Decision: Profile latency versus thread count instead of assuming monotonic benefit.
Paper_Title: Auto-reconfiguration for Latency Minimization in CPU-based DNN Serving
Authors: Ankit Bhardwaj; Amar Phanishayee; Deepak Narayanan; Ryan Stutsman
Research_Evidence: The study observes that intra-operator parallelism reduces latency but provides diminishing returns.
Limitations: No universal optimal thread count or diminishing-return threshold.

Rule_Name: CPU Serving Configuration Should Jointly Consider Instances, Threads, and Batch Size
Rule_Description: For CPU-based online DNN serving, treat model-instance count, threads per instance, and batch size as coupled configuration variables when optimizing latency.
Inputs: DNN model; CPU core count; instance count; threads per instance; batch size; latency
Condition: Online CPU inference is being configured for latency
Output_Decision: Search or profile the joint configuration space rather than tuning one variable in isolation.
Paper_Title: Auto-reconfiguration for Latency Minimization in CPU-based DNN Serving
Authors: Ankit Bhardwaj; Amar Phanishayee; Deepak Narayanan; Ryan Stutsman
Research_Evidence: Packrat jointly chooses instances, threads per instance, and batch sizes for latency minimization and states that configuration depends on model, batch size, and CPU-core deployment.
Limitations: Do not copy Packrat's empirical configurations as universal CPU settings.

Rule_Name: CPU Inference Comparisons Must Preserve Benchmark Scenario Context
Rule_Description: When CPU inference performance is compared or used as DSS evidence, retain model, scenario, implementation, batch/concurrency conditions, and measured metric so that comparisons remain reproducible and meaningful.
Inputs: Model; scenario; implementation; batch/concurrency; latency/throughput metric
Condition: Inference performance is benchmarked or compared
Output_Decision: Accept/compare results only with benchmark context retained.
Authors: Vijay Janapa Reddi; Christine Cheng; David Kanter; Peter Mattson; et al.
Research_Evidence: MLPerf establishes standardized inference benchmarking methods and emphasizes representative, reproducible comparisons across diverse systems.
Applicability: Inference benchmark evidence used for DSS comparison.
Limitations: Benchmark methodology does not provide a universal CPU capacity equation.
